newsitem.title: USA: SEC charges six in Royce insider case.
newsitem.headline: SEC charges six in Royce insider case.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Friday that it charged three executives of Royce Laboratories Inc and three others with insider trading for using non-public information on the generic drug Piroxicam.

In a civil complaint filed in a U.S. district court in Brooklyn, N.Y., the SEC alleged the defendants traded the Miami-based company's stock in the fall of 1991 and spring of 1992, resulting in illegal profits and losses avoided of over $142,638.

Helen Williams, an aide to Royce president Patrick McEnany, said McEnany had not seen the complaint and would not comment. She said the company was expected to issue a statement on Monday, September 9. The Royce executives and the other defendants could not be reached for comment.

The SEC alleged that executive vice president Abul Bhuiyan, quality control director Nilkanth Patel and chemist Hasmukh Patel bought Royce securities in September 1991 knowing the company was about to or had received tentative approval from regulators to market Piroxicam.
The SEC said it is seeking permanent injunctions, the return of all alleged illegal profits, plus prejudgment interest and illegal insider trading penalties against the defendants.

In May, Royce and McEnany settled a separate SEC civil lawsuit charging them with issuing a misleading press release about the status of the government's approval of Piroxicam. They settled without admitting or denying guilt.
